submission.justification: Sensor-T3 gives the best unirradiated single-hit resolution of the three candidates by a wide margin: about 6.0-6.4 um across 50-200 um, versus about 8.7-9.2 um for Sensor-T2 and about 14.2 um for Sensor-T1 (100-150 um). Within T3, the measured minimum is 5.96 um at 125 um, but the spread across 50-200 um (about 0.4 um) is comparable to run-to-run variation, so thickness is not a strong lever for resolution. The project documents contain no irradiated performance or radiation-tolerance data for any candidate, so radiation suitability cannot be confirmed from the available material. That is the main open risk. Thinner T3 (about 100 um) would be a reasonable alternative if irradiation studies favour lower depletion/trapping losses, at a negligible resolution cost. The recommendation is conditional on radiation qualification of T3 at HL-LHC fluences before final selection.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible single-hit spatial resolution in the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Simulated unirradiated resolution: T3 5.96 um at 125 um (range 5.96-6.44 um across 50-200 um) vs T2 8.7-9.2 um and T1 14.2 um. T3 is best at every thickness tested.
